/-!
# Erdős Problem 309

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/309](https://www.erdosproblems.com/309)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Yo97] Yokota, Hisashi, *On number of integers representable as a sum of unit fractions. II*.
  J. Number Theory (1997), 162--169.
- [Cr99] Croot, III, Ernest S., *On some questions of Erdős and Graham about Egyptian fractions*.
  Mathematika (1999), 359-372.
- [Yo02] Yokota, Hisashi, *On the number of integers representable as sums of unit fractions.
  III*. J. Number Theory (2002), 351--372.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Asymptotics Topology

namespace Erdos309

/-- The number of integers which can be written as the sum of distinct unit fractions with
denominators from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. -/
noncomputable def F (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  {m : ℕ | ∃ A : Finset ℕ, A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ ∑ n ∈ A, (1 / n : ℚ) = m}.ncard

/--
Let $N\geq 1$. How many integers can be written as the sum of distinct unit fractions with
denominators from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$? Are there $o(\log N)$ such integers?

If the number of such integers is $N(n)$ then it is trivial that $N(n)\leq \log n+O(1)$. Yokota
[Yo97] proved that $N(n)\geq \log n-O(\log\log n)$.

Croot [Cr99] proved that every integer at most
$$\leq \sum_{n\leq N}\frac{1}{n}-(\tfrac{9}{2}+o(1))\frac{(\log\log N)^2}{\log N}$$
can be so represented.

If $F(N)$ counts the number of integers which can be represented in this fashion, then the
current best lower bound known is
$$F(N) \geq \log N+\gamma -\left(\frac{\pi^2}{3}+o(1)\right)\frac{(\log\log N)^2}{\log N}$$
due to Yokota [Yo02].

The answer to the question is no: $F(N) \sim \log N$. Here $0$ (the empty sum) is counted.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos309.lean#L374"]
theorem erdos_309 : answer(False) ↔
    (fun N : ℕ => (F N : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun N : ℕ => Real.log N := by
  sorry

/-- The number of representable integers satisfies $F(N) \sim \log N$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos309.lean#L374"]
theorem erdos_309.variants.asymptotic :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (F N : ℝ) / Real.log N) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos309

reformulations.difference: Relative to Croot [Cr99] §1 and the positive-integer convention in [Yo97], F counts one additional integer: 0, represented by the empty finset. The file explicitly documents this convention. The original book's formulation with coefficients in {0,1} also permits the all-zero choice.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let P(N) count only positive represented integers. The represented set is finite, all its elements are nonnegative, and 0 is represented, so F(N)=P(N)+1. Since 1/log N tends to 0, F(N)=o(log N) iff P(N)=o(log N), and F(N)/log N tends to 1 iff P(N)/log N tends to 1. Both equivalences and the exact counting identity were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations. The original book asks how many integers are representable and whether their number could exceed c log n; Croot's bounds establish the leading asymptotic log n. Thus answer(False) has the correct polarity and the ratio-limit variant is faithful. The current community database records problem 309 as disproved (Lean), consistent with both solved tags and the cited external proof. Scratch checks establish finiteness of the set counted by ncard, positivity of every permitted denominator, equivalence of rational/real and natural/integer representability, and the harmlessness of log 0 and log 1 in these atTop statements. Computations and proofs give F(0)=1, F(1)=2, F(5)=2 and F(6)=3. The scratch file compiles without errors or warnings. Access limitations: the live erdosproblems.com page returned Cloudflare challenges, and Yokota's full texts could not be retrieved; their quantitative remarks were checked against the detailed zbMATH reviews instead. All Lean declarations were nevertheless settled against accessible cited primary literature.
